metadata.scenario: A home health aide calls the office in a panic because an elderly patient fell and hit their head. The patient is conscious but confused and has a bump forming. The aide asks what to do. The receptionist instructs her to call 911 immediately and stay with the patient.

transcription.text: Thank you for calling CareFirst Home Health, this is Margaret, how can I help you? Hi, Margaret, this is Jennifer Taylor. I need help right away! Of course, Jennifer. What’s going on? I’m at my grandmother's house, and she just fell and hit her head. Oh no! Is she conscious? Yes, but she seems confused and there's a bump forming. Okay, Jennifer, I need you to call 911 immediately. It's important. I will, but what should I do until they arrive? Stay with her and keep her calm. Don’t let her move too much. Okay, I can do that. What if she starts to feel worse? If she gets worse, keep her still and make sure to provide any information you can to the paramedics. Alright, I just called 911. They’ll be here soon. Good job, Jennifer. Is there anyone else nearby who can come help? Yes, my aunt is on her way. Should I tell her anything? Yes, inform her about the situation and that you've called for help. Got it. Should I consider getting a caregiver for my grandmother after this? Absolutely, we offer companion care that can assist with daily activities. That sounds great. I’d like to know more about that once things settle down. Of course! I can follow up with you about our companion care services. Thank you, I really appreciate your help right now. You're welcome, Jennifer. Just stay with your grandmother and keep her comfortable. I will. I’ll call back for that information once everything is okay. Sounds good. Take care and I hope she’s alright. Thank you, I hope so too. Goodbye. Goodbye, Jennifer.
